Least squares loss of an ODE model from modelcompR

Source: R/integration-modelcompR.R
opt_ode_loss.Rd

Builds the scalar expression \(\sum_{t, s} w_{ts} (u_s(t; \theta) - y_{ts})^2\) for an ODEProblem of the modelcompR package, with \(\theta\) given by decision variables. Each evaluation solves the ODE and its forward sensitivities (ODEForwardSensitivityProblem()), so the gradient is the exact derivative of the numerical solution up to the integration tolerances; no finite differences are used. Value and gradient at the same point share one solve.

Usage

opt_ode_loss(
  prob,
  theta,
  times,
  data,
  states = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  reltol = 1e-10,
  abstol = 1e-12,
  alg = NULL
)

Arguments

prob

A modelcompR ODEProblem; its parameters are replaced by theta.

theta

Decision variables (or an expression) for the ODE parameters, in the order the right-hand side uses them.

times

Observation times.

data

Matrix of observations, one row per time and one column per observed state (NA for missing values).

states

Indices of the observed states.

weights

Matrix of weights like data (default 1).

reltol, abstol

Integration tolerances.

alg

Integration algorithm (default modelcompR::Tsit5()).

Value

A scalar nonlinear opt_expr.

Details

The loss is generally not convex, so solves are local: start from a sensible start on the variables.

Examples

f <- function(u, p, t) -p[1] * u
prob <- modelcompR::ODEProblem(f, 1, c(0, 2), 1)
times <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2)
y <- matrix(exp(-0.8 * times), ncol = 1)
m <- opt_model()
k <- opt_variable(m, "k", lower = 0, upper = 5, start = 0.3)
opt_objective(m, opt_ode_loss(prob, k, times, y))
opt_value(opt_solve(m), k)  # 0.8
#> [1] 0.8
